subject.title: fix: CLI commands hang while checking large state databases

question: Should ordinary CLI and TUI startup prioritize fast current-schema preflight by deferring detection of unrelated index corruption to Doctor, while preserving full verification for migration, quarantine, and explicit repair paths?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the integrity-reporting contract for existing commands; tests can show the mechanics, but only maintainers can choose the acceptable detection and operator-safety boundary.

options.title: Accept the scoped CLI boundary
options.body: Approve the fast path after rebase, provided the resolved merge retains full verification for Doctor, migrations, quarantined databases, and gateway checkpoint owners.

options.title: Keep full CLI verification
options.body: Preserve immediate discovery of all integrity damage during ordinary command startup and accept the large-database startup delay until a different owner-safe design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped CLI boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the fast path after rebase, provided the resolved merge retains full verification for Doctor, migrations, quarantined databases, and gateway checkpoint owners.

likelyOwner.reason: This reviewer has already examined the precise cache and verification-boundary behavior affected by the proposal.
